title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll dealt Mission Control. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Mission Control
options.lineage: Apollo-era flight control room: projection wall, consoles, go/no-go
options.thesis: Eight years of production systems run like flights: launched, tracked live, brought home.
options.viewport: Full-bleed ultramarine projection wall. A live ground-track trace sweeps the world map past Cebu, Australia and the US: that is the moving background. JAMES DELOS REYES is set in big engraved console caps, with a three-lamp telemetry strip for 8+ years, 10+ systems and 5 industries. Primary action is a lit EMAIL / RESUME console key row.
options.risk: If the trace and the lamps get too cute it reads as a space-themed costume, not as proof.

raised.raise: Every metric is pinned by a leader line to the system it measures. No floating stat tiles.
The projection wall owns the whole first viewport as one saturated field. No neutral near-black ground.
Each mission (role or case study) gets its own patch: one cover, one composition.
Exactly one lamp is lit: the current mission reads IN FLIGHT and everything else is a logged flight.
Case studies run as fixed flight phases in order (problem, approach, outcome) with marked points, not tabs.

options.label: Transit Network Map
options.thesis: A career drawn as one transit network: every role a line, every shipped system a station, PH to AU to US.
options.viewport: The whole viewport is the network map. Trains run the lines as the moving background, the name sits on the map legend, and the stations are clickable systems.
options.risk: Familiar: transit-map résumés are a known infographic trope, and a light ground can drift corporate if the line colours are timid.

options.label: One-Bit Desktop
options.thesis: The portfolio as a 1-bit desktop: each system a window, dithered tone, marching-ants selection.
options.viewport: A dithered desktop with overlapping windows: about.txt open on top, case studies as folders, and the dither pattern drifting slowly.
options.case: Holds audience recognition (instantly techy), but it swaps one OS costume for another after you left the IDE.
options.risk: Desktop-OS portfolios are their own trope, and the costume can upstage the work.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: Work develops through fixed stations under amber safelight.
options.viewport: An amber field with a print emerging in the tray.
options.case: Hiring managers don't recognise themselves in a darkroom, and it says photographer, not engineer.
options.kept: Fixed stations in order: case studies run as flight phases with marked points.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: The stack as forces in balance.
options.viewport: A breathing column with force-value labels.
options.case: An abstract metaphor that's weak on both recognition and clarity.
options.kept: Leader-line annotations: metrics are pinned to what they measure.

options.label: Silk Color Chords
options.thesis: Overlapping silk lanes as computed states.
options.case: Beautiful, but it carries nothing about shipping systems.
options.kept: Total colour commitment: the wall is one saturated field.

options.label: Matchbook Drawer
options.thesis: Each place kept as a foil-stamped cover.
options.kept: One cover, one composition: a mission patch per role.

options.label: Cereal Aisle
options.thesis: Saturated box facings competing for your eye.
options.viewport: A wall of boxes at eye height.
options.case: Wrong register for senior engineering hiring.
options.kept: One violator: a single lit lamp marks the current mission.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark developer portfolio done impeccably: animated gradient-mesh background, big name, project cards.
canonCard.viewport: Centred name and role over a slow-moving gradient, with a CTA pair and a project card grid below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from thousands of dev portfolios by design.
